title: GMO Internet CEO Blames Autonomous AI Tool for Brokerage Cyberattack
summary:
Masatoshi Kumagai, CEO of GMO Internet Group, said an autonomous AI penetration-testing tool called ARTEX was abused to facilitate a cyberattack that targeted roughly 20 Japanese companies and breached the group's cloud VPS service. The intrusion allowed hackers to execute unauthorized trades across more than 70 securities and FX brokerages and exposed up to 26,739 servers to unauthorized access.

Kumagai admitted that the company's internal security team had flagged vulnerabilities in the breached service before the attack, but the fix was not implemented quickly enough. He characterized the incident as a national crisis and warned that the internet is on the verge of being destroyed by the misuse of AI. GMO has requested that the Japanese government use its active cyber defense powers, which went into effect Oct. 1, to trace and neutralize the attackers' infrastructure.

GMO also recieved a ransom demand, presumably to not release customer information. They have refused to pay. Over 26,000 servers may have been accessed. Timeline by Argon.

Quoting from GMO:

'Regarding this extortion, we have submitted all evidence, including communication records, to the police authorities (cybercrime countermeasures department).

We are requesting a thorough investigation as a criminal case.

Please note that attackers may in the future publish information they claim to be about our company or our customers.

 [Our response policy]

We will not comply with requests from attackers.

Even if we comply with your request, we cannot guarantee that the acquired information will be deleted or that it will not be misused.

We have consulted with the police and other relevant organizations regarding this matter, and we are working together to address it.

selectedTweets.text:
🚨Hackers have breached GMO Internet's cloud service used to run automated FX trading, planted malware on customer servers and stole customer information. Up to 26,739 servers may be affected, and users have reported trades they never made.

Now the attackers are demanding money and threatening to keep placing unauthorized orders to wipe balances across accounts at more than 70 securities and FX firms, leak customer data and launch ransomware attacks.

GMO says it will not pay. It is compensating verified trading losses and has asked Japan to make the attack the first case for its new active cyber defense powers, with the government tracing, blocking and neutralizing the attackers' infrastructure.

selectedTweets.text:
HOLY. GMO Internet Group CEO Masatoshi Kumagai says: 'Right now, the internet itself is starting to break.'

'In fact, an investigation by our group's GMO Cybersecurity by Ierae has confirmed that at the source of unauthorized access targeting roughly 20 Japanese companies, 'ARTEX,' an autonomous AI penetration-testing tool originally meant for defense, was being abused.'

The breach exposed up to 26,739 servers and trading accounts across 70+ brokerages and FX firms. GMO has asked Japan to apply its new Active Cyber Defense law, in force since October 1.

'We have already entered an era where, with just simple instructions, AI searches for weaknesses and runs all the way to intrusion on its own.'
